claim: Legionella pneumophila extensively modulates the host ubiquitin network to create the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) for its replication.
source: Legionella pneumophila extensively modulates the host ubiquitin network to create the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) for its replication.
evidence: This is a general statement about L. pneumophila's interaction with host cells, drawing from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Many L. pneumophila virulence factors function as ubiquitin ligases or deubiquitinases (DUBs).
source: Many of its virulence factors function as ubiquitin ligases or deubiquitinases (DUBs).
evidence: This statement is supported by references to prior research on L. pneumophila effectors.

claim: Lem27 is a DUB that displays a preference for diubiquitin formed by K6, K11, or K48.
source: Here, we identify Lem27 as a DUB that displays a preference for diubiquitin formed by K6, K11, or K48.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing substrate specificity in Figure 4.

claim: Lem27 is associated with the LCV where it regulates Rab10 ubiquitination in concert with SidC and SdcA.
source: Lem27 is associated with the LCV where it regulates Rab10 ubiquitination in concert with SidC and SdcA, two bacterial E3 ubiquitin ligases.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3 and biochemical assays in Figure 7.

claim: Structural analysis reveals that Lem27 harbors a fold resembling those in the OTU1 DUB subfamily with a Cys-His catalytic dyad.
source: Structural analysis of the complex formed by an active fragment of Lem27 and the substrate-based suicide inhibitor ubiquitin-propargylamide (PA) reveals that it harbors a fold resembling those in the OTU1 DUB subfamily with a Cys-His catalytic dyad
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data and structural analysis presented in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Lem27 recognizes ubiquitin via extensive hydrogen bonding at six contact sites.
source: it recognizes ubiquitin via extensive hydrogen bonding at six contact sites.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Lem27 functions to regulate protein ubiquitination on L. pneumophila phagosomes by counteracting the activity of bacterial ubiquitin E3 ligases.
source: Our results establish Lem27 as a DUB that functions to regulate protein ubiquitination on L. pneumophila phagosomes by counteracting the activity of bacterial ubiquitin E3 ligases.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7 showing the interplay between Lem27 and SidC family ligases.

claim: L. pneumophila is an opportunistic pathogen ubiquitously found in natural and man-made water systems, often by association with amoebae species.
source: The Gram negative bacterium Legionella pneumophila is an opportunistic pathogen ubiquitously found in natural and man-made water systems, often by association with amoebae species (Fields et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fields et al., 2002.

claim: Infection of humans by L. pneumophila occurs when susceptible individuals inhale contaminated aerosols.
source: Infection of humans by L. pneumophila occurs when susceptible individuals inhale contaminated aerosols, which introduce the bacteria to the lungs where alveolar macrophages engulf them by phagocytosis (Newton et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Newton et al., 2010.

claim: The bacterial phagosome called the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) initiates a trafficking route that bypasses the endocytic maturation pathway.
source: The bacterial phagosome called the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) initiates a trafficking route that bypasses the endocytic maturation pathway (Xu and Luo, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Xu and Luo, 2013.

claim: The LCV appears to intercept vesicles originating from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and is eventually converted into a compartment whose membranes resemble those of the ER.
source: Instead, it appears to intercept vesicles originating from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and is eventually converted into a compartment whose membranes resemble those of the ER (Swanson and Isberg, 1995; Tilney et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Swanson and Isberg, 1995 and Tilney et al., 2001.

claim: The conversion of the plasma membranes from nascent phagosomes into the LCV with ER properties is largely mediated by virulence factors delivered via the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system.
source: The conversion of the plasma membranes from nascent phagosomes into the LCV with ER properties largely is mediated by virulence factors delivered into host cells via the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system of L. pneumophila (Isberg et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Isberg et al., 2009.

claim: L. pneumophila effectors interfere with diverse cellular processes including membrane trafficking, autophagy, protein translation and immunity by diverse mechanisms.
source: These virulence factors, also called effectors, interfere with such diverse cellular processes as membrane trafficking, autophagy, protein translation and immunity by diverse mechanisms (Qiu and Luo, 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Qiu and Luo, 2017a.

claim: The modulation of cellular processes is mediated by targeting key regulatory proteins via effector-induced post-translational modifications, including phosphorylation, methylation, phosphorylcholination, AMPylation, and ubiquitination.
source: The modulation of these processes is mediated by targeting key regulatory proteins via effector-induced post-translational modifications, including phosphorylation (Haenssler and Isberg, 2011), methylation (Rolando et al., 2013), phosphorylcholination (Mukherjee et al., 2011; Tan et al., 2011), AMPylation (Hardiman and Roy, 2014; Müller et al., 2010; Tan and Luo, 2011), and ubiquitination (Qiu and Luo, 2017b)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on different post-translational modifications.

claim: L. pneumophila effectors subvert the metabolism of lipids key in cell signaling, including the production of phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI4P) on the LCV.
source: or by subverting the metabolism of lipids key in cell signaling (Swart and Hilbi, 2020), including the production of phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI4P) on the LCV (Hsu et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Swart and Hilbi, 2020 and Hsu et al., 2012.

claim: L. pneumophila effectors remove phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate from distinct organelles by phospholipase or PI phosphatases.
source: and the removal of phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate from distinct organelles by phospholipase (Gaspar and Machner, 2014) or PI phosphatases (Toulabi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gaspar and Machner, 2014 and Toulabi et al., 2013.

claim: More than 10 Dot/Icm effectors have been found to function as ubiquitin E3 ligases via various mechanisms.
source: More than 10 Dot/Icm effectors have been found to function as ubiquitin E3 ligases via various mechanisms (Qiu and Luo, 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Qiu and Luo, 2017b.

claim: Some L. pneumophila E3 ligases possess structural domains such as F-box and U-box found in components of mammalian E3 ligase complex.
source: Some of these proteins possess structural domains such as F-box and U-box found in components of mammalian E3 ligase complex (Ensminger and Isberg, 2010; Habyarimana et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2015; Kubori et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on F-box and U-box containing effectors.

claim: Some L. pneumophila E3 ligases harbor cryptic motifs that catalyze the ubiquitin ligation reaction by unique mechanisms.
source: whereas others harbor cryptic motifs that catalyze the ubiquitin ligation reaction by unique mechanisms (Hsu et al., 2014; Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hsu et al., 2014 and Lin et al., 2018.

claim: Members of the SidE effector family catalyze phosphoribosyl ubiquitination on serine residues of several small Rab GTPases and of the ER protein Rtn4 by a NAD-dependent mechanism that bypasses the host E1 and E2 enzymes.
source: Most unexpectedly, members of the SidE effector family catalyze phosphoribosyl ubiquitination on serine residues of several small Rab small GTPases and of the ER protein Rtn4 by a NAD-dependent mechanism that bypasses the host E1 and E2 enzymes (Bhogaraju et al., 2016; Kotewicz et al., 2017; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bhogaraju et al., 2016, Kotewicz et al., 2017, and Qiu et al., 2016.

claim: The activity of SidE family ubiquitin ligases is regulated by bacterial enzymes that function either to reverse the ubiquitination or to directly block the ubiquitin activation step of the catalysis by calmodulin-dependent glutamylation.
source: Interestingly, the activity of these unique ubiquitin ligases is regulated by bacterial enzymes that function either to reverse the ubiquitination (Shin et al., 2020; Wan et al., 2019) or to directly block the ubiquitin activation step of the catalysis by calmodulin-dependent glutamylation (Bhogaraju et al., 2019; Black et al., 2019; Gan et al., 2019b; Sulpizio et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent studies on SidE regulation.

claim: Ubiquitination can be reversed by specific deubiquitinases (DUBs), which are a large group of proteases functioning to cleave ubiquitin moieties from modified substrates.
source: Ubiquitination can be reversed by specific deubiquitinases (DUBs), which are a large group of proteases functioning to cleave ubiquitin moieties from modified substrates (Komander and Rape, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Komander and Rape, 2012.

claim: The activity of DUBs restores ubiquitinated proteins back to their original forms thereby reversing the effects caused by ubiquitination.
source: The activity of DUBs restores ubiquitinated proteins back to their original forms thereby reversing the effects caused by ubiquitination.
evidence: This is a general statement about DUB function based on established knowledge.

claim: Coordinated activity of E3 ubiquitin ligases and DUBs controls the fate of modified substrates.
source: Coordinated activity of E3 ubiquitin ligases and DUBs thus controls the fate of modified substrates (Popovic et al., 2014; Qiu and Luo, 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Popovic et al., 2014 and Qiu and Luo, 2017b.

claim: DUBs are classified into several subfamilies, including ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs), ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases (UCHs), ovarian tumor proteases (OTUs), Machado-Joseph disease protein domain proteases (MJDS), JAMM/MPN domain-associated metallopeptidases (JAMMs), and the more recently identified MINDY and ZFUSP family of DUBs.
source: According to their structures and mechanisms of action, DUBs are classified into several subfamilies, including ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs), ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases (UCHs), ovarian tumor proteases (OTUs) (Balakirev et al., 2003), Machado-Joseph disease protein domain proteases (MJDS), JAMM/MPN domain-associated metallopeptidases(JAMMs) (Ronau et al., 2016) and the more recently identified MINDY and ZFUSP family of DUBs (Abdul Rehman et al., 2016; Hermanns et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on DUB classification.

claim: Pathogens employ DUBs to hijack host cellular processes for their benefits.
source: In addition to ubiquitin ligases, pathogens also employ DUBs to hijack host cellular processes for their benefits (Wilkinson, 2009)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wilkinson, 2009.

claim: A number of DUBs have been found in L. pneumophila.
source: and a number of DUBs have been found in L. pneumophila (Kitao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kitao et al., 2020.

claim: Members of the SidE effector family harbor DUB activity in a domain that encompasses their first 200 residues, which appears to exhibit preference for K63-linked ubiquitin chains.
source: Among these, members of the SidE effector family harbor DUB activity in a domain that encompasses their first 200 residues, which appears to exhibit preference for K63-linked ubiquitin chains (Sheedlo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sheedlo et al., 2015.

claim: LotA is a DUB with two distinct catalytic domains, one of which functions to cleave K6-linked polyubiquitins specifically and the other displaying general DUB activity toward polyubiquitins regardless of their structure.
source: LotA is a DUB with two distinct catalytic domains, one of which functions to cleave K6-linked polyubiquitins specifically and the other displaying general DUB activity toward polyubiquitins regardless of their structure (Kubori et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kubori et al., 2018.

claim: Ceg23 is a DUB that exclusively cleaves K63-linked polyubiquitin chains.
source: More recently, we have identified Ceg23 as a DUB that exclusively cleaves K63-linked polyubiquitin chains (Ma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ma et al., 2020.

claim: Lem27 (Lpg2529) harbors a motif distantly similar to members of the OTU superfamily of DUBs.
source: This exercise led to the identification of Lem27 (Lpg2529) which harbors a motif distantly similar to members of the OTU superfamily of DUBs.
evidence: This is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Lem27 displays a broader activity toward ubiquitin chain types with a distinct preference for K6-, K11- and K48-type polyubiquitin chains.
source: Our results demonstrate that Lem27 displays a broader activity toward ubiquitin chain types with a distinct preference for K6-, K11- and K48-type polyubiquitin chains.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Lem27 harbors an OTU1 fold.
source: Structural analysis reveals that Lem27 harbors an OTU1 fold
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data in Figure 5.

claim: Lem27 recognizes ubiquitin via interactions mediated by at least six contact sites.
source: and that it recognizes ubiquitin via interactions mediated by at least six contact sites.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis in Figure 6.

claim: Lem27 coordinates with the SidC family E3 ligases to regulate protein ubiquitination on the surface of bacterial phagosomes.
source: We also provide evidence to show that Lem27 coordinates with the SidC family E3 ligases to regulate protein ubiquitination on the surface of bacterial phagosomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: Cys24 and two adjacent residues of Lem27 constitute a conserved Gly-Asn-Cys tripeptide motif shared among several cysteine proteases involved in the regulation of modifications by ubiquitin or the ubiquitin-like ISG15.
source: Sequence alignment produced by the HHpred algorithm suggests that Cys24 and two adjacent residues of Lem27 constitutes a conserved Gly-Asn-Cys tripeptide motif shared among several cysteine proteases involved in the regulation of modifications by ubiquitin or the ubiquitin-like ISG15 from humans or viral pathogens (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Incubation of Lem27 with Ub-PA led to the formation of a covalent conjugate characterized by an approximately 8 kDa increase in its molecular weight.
source: Incubation of Lem27 with Ub-PA led to the formation of a covalent conjugate typical for reactive DUBs, which is characterized by an approximately 8 kDa increase in its molecular weight (Figure 2a, lower panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Lem27C24A has lost the ability to react with Ub-PA.
source: This mutant has lost the ability to react with Ub-PA (Figure 2a, lower panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Lem27 is a DUB which uses Cys24 for catalysis.
source: These results suggest that Lem27 is a DUB which uses Cys24 for catalysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the Ub-PA reactivity data in Figure 2a.

claim: In cells coexpressing GFP-Lem27 or GFP-SdeADUB, ubiquitinated proteins were considerably reduced compared to cells coexpressing GFP alone.
source: In contrast, although Flag-Ub was expressed at comparable levels, ubiquitinated proteins in cells coexpressing GFP-Lem27 or GFP-SdeADUB were considerably reduced (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Purified His6-Lem27 but not its inactive mutant His6-Lem27C24A effectively removed ubiquitin from proteins ubiquitinated by Flag-Ub.
source: In agreement with the DUB activity observed in the cotransfection experiments, purified His6-Lem27 but not its inactive mutant His6-Lem27C24A effectively removed ubiquitin from proteins ubiquitinated by Flag-Ub that were isolated from cells by immunoprecipitation (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The LCV is enriched with ubiquitinated proteins.
source: The LCV is enriched with ubiquitinated proteins (Dorer et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dorer et al., 2006.

claim: Ubiquitinated proteins on the LCV are likely dynamically regulated by enzymes involved in ubiquitination from both the host and the pathogen.
source: which likely is dynamically regulated by enzymes involved in ubiquitination from both the host and the pathogen.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the presence of both host and bacterial ubiquitination machinery.

claim: Flag-Lem27 was detected in the saponin-soluble fraction of U937 cells infected with a strain harboring a functional Dot/Icm system but not a strain lacking an active Dot/Icm transporter.
source: Flag-Lem27 was detected in the saponin-soluble fraction of U937 cells infected with a strain harboring a functional Dot/Icm system but not a strain lacking an active Dot/Icm transporter (Figure 3a)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Lem27 is translocated into host cells by the Dot/Icm transporter during L. pneumophila infection.
source: validating that Lem27 is translocated into host cells by the Dot/Icm transporter during L. pneumophila infection.
evidence: This is inferred from the saponin fractionation data in Figure 3a.

claim: Approximately 80% of LCVs containing L. pneumophila with a functional Dot/Icm system stained positive for 4xFlag-Lem27.
source: Such association only occurred in cells infected with the L. pneumophila strain harboring a functional Dot/Icm system, with approximately 80% staining positive for the fusion protein (Figure 3b–c).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3b-c.

claim: Association of Lem27 with vacuoles was not detected in cells infected with the dotA- strain.
source: Although 4xFlag-Lem27 was similarly expressed in the dotA- strain, association of the Lem27 with its vacuoles was not detected (Figure 3b–c).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3b-c.

claim: Approximately 80% of the vacuoles in D. discoideum infected with the strain expressing a functional Dot/Icm system stained positive for Lem27.
source: For the strain expressing a functional Dot/Icm system, approximately 80% of the vacuoles stained positive for Lem27 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: No association of Lem27 with vacuoles was detected in D. discoideum samples infected with the strain lacking a functional transporter.
source: and no such association was detected in samples infected with the strain lacking a functional transporter (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Close to 40% of the vacuoles containing the wild-type strain Lp02 stained positive by the FK1 antibody specific for ubiquitinated proteins.
source: As expected, close to 40% of the vacuoles containing the wild-type strain Lp02 stained positive by the antibody and no staining signal was detected in vacuoles containing the dotA- mutant Lp03 (Figure 3d–e).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3d-e.

claim: No ubiquitin staining signal was detected in vacuoles containing the dotA- mutant Lp03.
source: As expected, close to 40% of the vacuoles containing the wild-type strain Lp02 stained positive by the antibody and no staining signal was detected in vacuoles containing the dotA- mutant Lp03 (Figure 3d–e).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3d-e.

claim: A significant increase in the percentage of vacuoles positive for ubiquitin was observed in infections with the strain lacking the lem27 gene.
source: Importantly, we observed a significant increase in the percentage of vacuoles positive for ubiquitin in infections with the strain lacking the lem27 gene (Figure 3d and f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3d and f.

claim: Expression of lem27 but not the catalytically inactive mutant lem27C24A in the mutant strain from a plasmid restored the percentage of ubiquitin-positive vacuoles to wild-type levels.
source: Furthermore, expression of lem27 but not the catalytically inactive mutant lem27C24A in the mutant strain from a plasmid restored the percentage of association to wild-type levels (Figure 3d and f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3d and f.

claim: Similar results were obtained when the intensity of the ubiquitin staining signal was examined.
source: Similar results were obtained when the intensity of the ubiquitin staining signal was examined (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Lem27 functions to regulate protein ubiquitination on the LCV.
source: These results indicate that Lem27 functions to regulate protein ubiquitination on the LCV.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing increased ubiquitination on LCVs in the lem27 deletion mutant.

claim: Lem27 was readily detectable in freshly diluted bacteria, which was maintained at similar levels into the exponential phase.
source: Lem27 was readily detectable in freshly diluted bacteria, which was maintained at similar levels into the exponential phase.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Lem27 protein level began to increase when the culture entered later exponential phase (12 hr) and peaked at the stationary phase.
source: The protein level began to increase when the culture entered later exponential phase (12 hr) and peaked at the stationary phase (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Similar to many Dot/Icm substrates, lem27 is induced in bacteria of the transmissive state.
source: Thus, similar to many Dot/Icm substrates (Nagai et al., 2002; Luo and Isberg, 2004; VanRheenen et al., 2006), lem27 is induced in bacteria of the transmissive state
evidence: This is supported by the expression pattern data and citations to similar effectors.

claim: Lem27 may contribute to overcome host defense in the initial phase of infection.
source: which may contribute to overcome host defense in the initial phase of infection.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the expression pattern of Lem27.

claim: Given its relatively high-level expression at other growth phases, including the exponential phase, Lem27 likely also plays a role in other stages of the intracellular life cycle of L. pneumophila.
source: In addition, given its relatively high-level expression at other growth phases, including the exponential phase (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), Lem27 likely also plays a role in other stages of the intracellular life cycle of L. pneumophila.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the expression pattern data.

claim: The ∆lem27 mutant grew indistinguishably to that of the wild-type strain in both RAW264.7 macrophages and D. discoideum.
source: The mutant grew indistinguishably to that of the wild-type strain in both hosts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3a–c)
evidence: This is supported by intracellular growth assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3a-c.

claim: Deletion of lem27 did not detectably affect intracellular replication of the bacterium in laboratory infection models.
source: indicating that similarly to the majority of characterized Dot/Icm substrates, deletion of lem27 did not detectably affect intracellular replication of the bacterium in laboratory infection models.
evidence: This is inferred from the intracellular growth data.

claim: The strain Lp02∆lotA∆lem27 did not display detectable growth defects in either mammalian macrophages or D. discoideum.
source: This strain Lp02∆lotA∆lem27, did not display detectable growth defects in either mammalian macrophages or D. discoideum (Figure 3—figure supplement 3d).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular growth assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3d.

claim: In reactions containing 1.5 μM substrate and 1.0 μM His6-Lem27, approximately 50% of the diubiquitin linked at K6, K11 or K48 was efficiently cleaved in 10 min.
source: In reactions containing 1.5 μM substrate and 1.0 μM His6-Lem27, approximately 50% of the diubiquitin linked at K6, K11 or K48-linked diubiquitin substrates was efficiently cleaved in 10 min.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: In the same reaction time, approximately 35% of diubiquitins linked at K63 or K33 was cleaved.
source: In the same reaction time, approximately 35% of diubiquitins linked at K63 or K33 in the reactions was cleaved
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Cleavage of diubiquitin linked at K27 or K29 was barely detectable in 10 min reactions.
source: and cleavage of diubiquitin linked at K27 or K29 was barely detectable (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: When the reactions were allowed to proceed for 2 hr, cleavage of K6-linked diubiquitin was close to 80%.
source: When the reactions were allowed to proceed for 2 hr, cleavage of K6-linked diubiquitin was close to 80%
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Diubiquitins linked at K63 or K33 were cleaved to about 65% in 2 hr reactions.
source: those linked at K63 or K33 were cleaved to about 65%
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The cleavage of K27-linked diubiquitin was around 15% in 2 hr reactions.
source: and the cleave of K27-linked diubiquitin was around 15%.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Extension of the reaction time to 2 hr only led to negligible cleavage of K29-linked diubiquitin.
source: Extension of the reaction time to 2 hr only led to negligible cleavage of K29-linked diubiquitin (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Cleavage of M1-linked linear diubiquitin could not be detected even in reactions that were allowed to proceed for 2 hr.
source: Similarly, cleavage of M1-linked linear diubiquitin could not be detected even in reactions that were allowed to proceed for 2 hr (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The catalytically inactive mutant Lem27C24A has lost the ability to cleave any of the diubiquitin substrates.
source: As expected, the catalytically inactive mutant Lem27C24A has lost the ability to cleave any of these substrates (Figure 4a–b).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a-b.

claim: Lem27 exhibits certain degree of selectivity toward its substrates, with a preference for polyubiquitin chains linked at K6, K11, or K48, followed by K33- and K63- types.
source: Thus, Lem27 exhibits certain degree of selectivity toward its substrates, with a preference for polyubiquitin chains linked at K6, K11, or K48, followed by K33- and K63- types.
evidence: This is inferred from the substrate cleavage data in Figure 4a.

claim: Diubiquitin linked at K29 and linear diubiquitin cannot be cleaved by Lem27.
source: In contrast, diubiquitin linked at K29 and linear diubiquitin cannot be cleaved by Lem27 (Figure 4a–b).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4a-b.

claim: The Lem271-417 truncation mutant remained active against diubiquitin.
source: We found that the full-length Lem27 construct has the propensity to form aggregates of different sizes in solution, we therefore examined several carboxyl-terminal truncation mutants of which the Lem271-417 construct remained active against diubiquitin (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The structure of the Lem271-417-Ub-PA complex was solved to a resolution of 2.43 Å by single-wavelength anomalous diffraction (SAD) phasing.
source: Upon subjecting the complex formed by selenomethionine-labeled Lem271-417 and Ub-PA to crystallization screening, we obtained crystals and solved the structure to a resolution of 2.43 Å by single-wavelength anomalous diffraction (SAD) phasing (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: There are two copies of the Lem271-417-Ub-PA complex in an asymmetric unit (ASU).
source: There are two copies of the Lem271-417-Ub-PA complex in an asymmetric unit (ASU)(Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: There is no intermolecular interaction between the two Lem271-417 molecules in the ASU.
source: However, structural analysis suggests that there is no intermolecular interaction between these two Lem271-417 molecules
evidence: This is inferred from PISA analysis of the crystal structure.

claim: The two DUB modules of Lem271-417 molecules in an ASU are almost identical with a root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 0.249 Å over Cα atoms of 407 residues.
source: The two DUB modules of Lem271-417 molecules in an ASU are almost identical with a root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 0.249 Å over Cα atoms of 407 residues (residues 1–417)
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis of the crystal structure.

claim: There is an approximate 35° rotation of a domain consisting of a bundle of four α-helices (α-bundles) formed by α13-α16 spanning residues 315–417 between the two molecules in the ASU.
source: except that there is an approximate 35o rotation of a domain consisting of a bundle of four α-helices (α-bundles) formed by α13-α16 spanning residues 315–417 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The α-bundles collectively behave as a rigid body with an RMSD about 0.51 Å over Cα of 97 residues.
source: However, these α-bundles collectively behave as a rigid body with an RMSD about 0.51 Å over Cα of 97 residues
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: The linker between the α-bundles and the DUB domain is flexible.
source: implying that the linker between the α-bundles and the DUB domain is flexible (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis showing rotation of the α-bundle domain.

claim: The Lem271-417 molecule is composed of two distinct domains: a DUB domain spanning the first ~300 amino acids (residues 1–314) and a separate domain consisting of the four α-bundles (residues 315–417).
source: The Lem271-417 molecule is composed of two distinct domains (Figure 5a): a DUB domain spanning the first ~300 amino acids (residues 1–314) and a separate domain consisting of the four α-bundles (residues 315–417) (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5a-b.

claim: The DUB module with a bilobal architecture assumes the shape of the right hand.
source: The DUB module with a bilobal architecture assumes the shape of the right hand with one of the lobes giving the appearance of the thumb and forefinger and the other lobe as palm plus the three other fingers (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is a description of the structural features shown in Figure 5b.

claim: One lobe of the DUB module is composed of six α-helices (1–4, 10, and 11) and five β-strands (1-5).
source: One lobe is composed of six α-helices (1–4, 10, and 11) and five β-strands (1-5) where the strands form two separate β-sheets: one comprising of strands 1–3 and the other is an antiparallel β-hairpin (strands 4 and 5) which protrudes out from the rest of the mixed α-β core in this lobe (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The second lobe of the DUB module is composed of five α-helices α5 to α9, which form the fingers part of the hand.
source: The second lobe is composed of five α-helices α5 to α9, which form the fingers part of the hand (finger lobe).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: A vinylthioether bond is installed between the side chain of Cys24 from Lem271-417 and the propargylamide reactive end of Ub-PA.
source: A vinylthioether bond is installed between the side chain of Cys24 from Lem271-417 and the propargylamide reactive end of Ub-PA (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5c.

claim: His304 is found within 3.8 Å of the S-atom of the catalytic Cys24.
